## Security fixes: private-send IPC and bounded presence state

### Upgrade guidance

Upgrade the CLI and restart all running daemons before using private messaging.

A v0.1.12 CLI using `send --to` with a still-running v0.1.11 daemon could broadcast the intended private message to the topic: the older daemon ignored the recipient field on the shared broadcast IPC command. If you used this combination, treat those messages as disclosed to topic participants. Updating only the daemon does not fix an old CLI on other installations.

### Fixes

- Private sends now use a distinct `private_send` IPC command. The CLI checks the daemon's `private_send_v1` capability before submitting the body; older daemons fail safely with upgrade/restart guidance.
- Daemons reject ambiguous legacy broadcast requests carrying a recipient. Private acceptance responses are strictly validated, with no broadcast fallback or retry.
- Dynamic presence state, including replay watermarks, is capped at 1,024 identities. Expiry cleanup runs before admission and every 15 seconds without requiring client activity.
- New endpoint snapshots replace old presence addresses instead of accumulating them. A dedicated presence lookup isolates expiry from invite/bootstrap and attachment-ticket routes.
- Presence processing is rate-limited by authenticated Gossip transport hop, with bounded limiter state.
- CI and release validation now run direct-message and checksum-pinned v0.1.11/v0.1.12 IPC compatibility integration tests.

Normal broadcast IPC remains compatible. Private acknowledgements still mean volatile daemon acceptance, not durable delivery or human reading. Aliases remain self-asserted and are not continuity-pinned.

### Known remaining limitations

The previously identified startup failure when a new daemon bootstraps exclusively through older peers is not addressed in this release. Upgrade bootstrap peers as well. Recovery from mismatched alias state after interrupted forced initialization also remains separate work.

### Install

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg/main/install.sh | bash
```

Restart running daemons after installation. Or install this exact source release:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg.git \
  --tag v0.1.13 --locked --force
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Eldar-Ahmadov/meshmsg/compare/v0.1.12...v0.1.13
